title: Geometric Spin-Orbit Coupling Resolves the Contradictory CISS Effect in Chiral Single Molecules
authors: Shu-Zheng Zhou, Xi Sun, Kai-Yuan Zhang, Hua-Hua Fu
abstract: Some studies have reported clear chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect in four classes of chiral single molecules with remarkable spin polarization. In contrast, a recent high-precision measurement involving nearly a thousand individual tests failed to detect significant CISS signals in the same molecular systems (J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2025, \textbf{147}, 25043). These conflicting results cast doubt on whether CISS truly occurs in these chiral systems at the single-molecular level. To resolve this discrepancy, we develop a theoretical framework incorporating geometric spin-orbit coupling and environmental decoherence, enabling systematic study of the CISS in four chiral single molecules with distinct geometries and sizes. Our calculations show that the CISS effect is completely suppressed in both strong-coherence and strong-decoherence regimes, but becomes pronounced in the intermediate-decoherence regime, where observable spin polarization emerges. In the strong-coherence regime, both electron-electron interaction and electron-vibration coupling enhance the CISS effect: the former is more effective in large molecules, whereas the latter plays a more significant role in smaller ones. Increasing temperature further enhances spin polarization. The proposed mechanism unifies contradictory experimental observations and reveals how the CISS effect evolves from regular helical (helical symmetric) to irregular helical (point-symmetric or axially symmetric) chirality. This framework thus provides a basis for unifying CISS phenomena across single-molecule systems, regardless of their specific molecular configurations or symmetry classes.
summary: This theoretical work resolves contradictions in CISS measurements by introducing geometric spin-orbit coupling into the analysis. The framework predicts that measurable spin polarization only occurs within an intermediate regime of environmental decoherence. It provides a unified understanding of CISS across various chiral molecular structures.
main_problem: The paper aims to resolve conflicting experimental reports regarding the Chirality-Induced Spin Selectivity (CISS) effect in chiral single molecules.
main_result: It shows that CISS is suppressed in both strong-coherence and strong-decoherence regimes, becoming pronounced only in an intermediate decoherence regime. The mechanism unifies observations by incorporating geometric spin-orbit coupling.
method: The authors developed a theoretical framework using tight-binding models to incorporate geometric SOC and environmental decoherence into the Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system involves chiral single molecules modeled as helical chains (e.g., cone-shaped, uniform helix). The theory incorporates molecular Hamiltonians augmented by geometric SOC terms and environmental decoherence via a master equation approach.
key_observables: Spin Polarization (SP), which is calculated using the Landauer-Büttiker formalism; $	ext{SP}_{\max}$ dependence on temperature and coupling strengths.
important_parameters: Decoherence strength ($\Gamma_d$), electron-vibration coupling constant ($	ilde{\lambda}_{	ext{e-vib}}$), and molecular geometry parameters (radius, pitch).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that geometric SOC provides the necessary theoretical extension beyond traditional intrinsic or field-driven SOC models to explain CISS.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate three types of SOC mechanisms; one shows SP for different molecular geometries across varying parameters; another presents phase diagrams mapping observable CISS to intermediate decoherence regimes.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the conflict in experimental data, then develops a theoretical framework incorporating geometric SOC and decoherence. It systematically calculates SP for various chiral models (A, B, C) under different coupling conditions ($	ext{e-vib}$, $	ext{e-e}$), concluding with generalized phase diagrams.
why_interesting: The explicit modeling of spin transport in nanoscale molecular junctions using geometric SOC and decoherence provides a rich platform for studying open quantum systems dynamics, particularly how environmental coupling dictates observable quantum effects like spin polarization.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Three SOC mechanisms that can be used to explain the generation of spin polarization. (a) Type-I: Atomic intrinsic SOC between different P-orbital components (e.g., Px, Py, Pz). (b) Type-II: Effective field-driven SOC from the electrons moving along the chiral paths, equivalent to an external electric field ⃗Eex=-∇U applied to the system. (c) Type-III: Geometric SOC due to the relativistic effect for electrons moving on curved paths.

Figure 2. Spin polarization for three chiral chain geometries along with the transport device configuration, local coordinate vectors and spatial curvature. (a) Three representative single-chiral chain geometries: cone-shaped (Model A), uniform (Model B), and progressive-pitch (Model C). (b) Transport device based on Model C, coupled to two nonmagnetic electrodes. The local tangent (⃗Ti), normal ( ⃗Ni) and binormal ( ⃗Bi) vectors are shown in red, green and magenta, respectively. (c) Spatial variation of the curvature κ in the three helix models. d-f Spin polarization versus energy E for Model A (Ω=0.4), Model B (Ω=α=0), and Model C (α=0.20).

Figure 3. Phase diagram of spin polarization versus the decoherence strength log10(Γd/t1) and the energy E for four types of chiral molecular junctions based on a half-turn (a), a full-turn (b), a one-and-a-half-turn (c), and a two-turn helix (d). Three contour lines for SP=1.0%, 10.0% and 20.0% are plotted.

Figure 4. Phase diagram of spin polarization and the maximum SP under electron-electron correction. (a)-(d) Phase diagrams of SP for four CSM-based junctions as functions of decoherence strength log10(Γd/t1) and onsite energy E, calculated at U=0.05t1. Contour lines are shown for SP=1.0%, 10.0% and 20.0%. (e)-(h) Maximum SP (SPmax) for the same four junctions as a function of E, for Hubbard U = 0, 0.01, and 0.05t1. The decoherence strength and temperature are fixed at Γd=5.0×10−4t1 and 300 K, respectively.

Figure 5. Phase diagrams of spin polarization and maximum SP under electron-vibration coupling. (a)-(d) Phase diagrams of SP for four CSM-based junctions as functions of log10(Γd/t1) and onsite energy E, calculated with electron-vibration coupling (˜λe−vib=0.08 or 0.20 t1 · nm) and without electron-electron correlation (U=0). Contour lines are shown for SP=1.0%, 10.0%, and 20.0%. (e)-(h) Maximum SP (SPmax) as a function of temperature for the same four junctions, for ˜λe−vib=0, 0.04, 0.08, and 0.1 (in unit of t1 · nm).
